name: Tehuelche
catalog_quote: The accent presents no difficulties, since it rests almost invariably on the first syllable, if a word consists of two, three or more syllables. [p. 4] Verba commencing with the syllable com, ca, ce, as com areshe, odabeuhe, cenauhe, are accented on the second syllable. Exceptions to these two rules will be found accented in the vocabulary. [p. 5, scanned de-garbled]

audit.recode_to: fixed-dominant (strict register OUT, dominant IN), rule vector unchanged 10 100 1000... read as root/stem-initial: stress on the first syllable of the (principal) morpheme, syllabic prefixes and first compound members unstressed, small lexical exception set - the Lango/Kalapuya treatment. Pin: Fernández Garay 1998a acento section (via Viegas Barros 2015:151-153 exx. 607-627 until the book is in hand) plus Schmid 1910 Part II p. 5. Also correct the p. 5 example forms in dq to 'cŏm areshc, că-abeshc, cĕ-nashc'.
audit.deciding_source_year: 1910 (1912 Actas printing; ms. based on 1859-63 fieldwork, first version 1860)
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote: p. 4 sentence verified verbatim on the held page image  and scanned text (line 31972); p. 5 rule verified on but the record's three example verbs are misreadings. (2) Deciding source is a 41-pp 19th-century missionary grammar sketch (fieldwork 1859-63, printed 1910/1912); Glottolog lists two modern full grammars by Fernández Garay (1993 thèse 488 pp; 1998 book 481 pp) and a phonology article (1996), none held. (3) The held Viegas Barros 2015 UBA thesis (pp. 151-153) relays Fernández Garay 1998a and Suárez: stress is fixed 'casi siempre' on the first syllable of the morpheme or principal morpheme; prefixed and compound forms carry stress on the second syllable (kaš-′č'ex, o-′ma:nk, ok-′wa:, mk′ma:), with further lexical exceptions (o′qaken 'ten', a′onek'enk).
